_about: Labelled cases for the Hot/Warm/Cold row (15 pts). Transcripts are written the way Soniox actually renders live speech - stray full stops, 'uh', mis-heard words - because that is what the classifier will see. Cases marked source 'pdf' use the four phrases the assignment publishes as what it will push us with; those are a must-pass gate, not an average. Hindi and Telugu cases appear in both romanised and native script, because Soniox returns either depending on the utterance. They count towards overall accuracy and towards the per-language breakdown, never towards the pdf gate.

_fields.label: expected hot|warm|cold
_fields.rule_forces: true if the deterministic overlay alone should force hot, with no model call
_fields.source: pdf = phrase published in the assignment (must-pass gate); pdf-translated = our Hindi/Telugu rendering of one of those four, which is NOT in the gate because we wrote it; ours = written by us
_fields.lang: en|hi|te|mixed - which language the LEAD speaks. 'mixed' is code-switched, which the scorecard names explicitly

cases._disputed: claude-opus-5 reads this as HOT: 'ready to commit immediately at a stated price point'. That is arguable - 'I am in' is commitment language, and twenty thousand is below our floor so there IS a budget barrier. The ACTION the assignment cares about probably favours the model: send this person the details now. Label left as warm deliberately - changing it to make the score look better is exactly the circularity the audit warned about. Decide before the live call.
